answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, with transition probabilities normalized by node degree and voting influence accumulated from trusted starting points. A sybil cluster isolated like a canyon behind a narrow cut has low conductance: few attestations cross its boundary, limiting walk entry and constraining its aggregate voting weight by external cut capacity rather than its number of fabricated identities. Trusted vault anchors and onyx-like adversarial nodes do not remove this min-cut bound.
